name: Example: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Matrix
problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/3e677aa7f2db1cc637e0566a60813ebae1e2bccf80325106317c1d2b7717c2a5.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/67a421166c674275ae14da43962c8e5c8ea37b6a9c8a0548d5b09428b703d831.png) are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/fde83769f627e95f5dfe3285bf275ebfe1678710a36c264b6662248063470bb0.png) then what is the value of $ad+eh?$
worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & -5-7\text{i} \\ 1-6\text{i} & 5-9\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 \\ -6 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $a=2,d=5,e=-3$ and $h=-9.$ Therefore,

$$
ad+eh=2 \cdot 5 + (-3) \cdot (-9) = 37.
$$
